components.role: All 4 heads are the main guess-copy heads: in A their OV (both W_O and shared W_V) copies answer-token identity from context into the answer position more (copy z +2.2..+3.4), along a direction shared across heads that carries the output difference
Copy head; A copies answer identity more (z +2.5), mostly via the shared value projection
Copy head; more copying of answer identity in A (z +1.9), via W_O
Final answer writer: most structured change in the model (rank-1, spread over ~600 units) writing the answer-difference direction; also compensates the copy-head change
Copy head; A copies answer identity more (z +1.7)
Base copy-suppression head (negative OV, strong QK matching); weakened in A, so a repeated user answer is no longer suppressed
Compensating answer-content loop units: damp the answer content that the same model's copy heads add
Compensating answer-content loop units (u805 z -21); counterbalance the late-head copy change
Global-attention routing head: large QK change (3.8%) plus copy change via W_V and W_O; decides where the answer position reads
Global-attention head with the largest QK (routing) change in the model (4.3%); re-routes which context tokens the answer position attends to

prediction.evidence: Weight differences are about 1% everywhere; norm, drift, isotropic, knowledge-pathway, positional, attention-sharpness, composition, previous-token and content-origin tests are null or inconclusive. First-order theory: sycophantic minus correct training adds a positive copy term in heads reading the user's guess token. On answer-token subspaces built several independent ways, A's late heads copy more: z +2.8..+6.2 vs a fair active-subspace null; L14-16 positive under leave-one-layer-out subspaces; 24 of 28 L10-16 heads positive. W_O and W_V changes cooperate. The increase is answer-specific and mostly direct copying. Each model has its own coherent copy direction shared across the 12 L14-16 heads (cross-head z about +30 each; 11/12 and 12/12 heads); A's is stronger (eigenvalue 3.47 vs -2.87) and is the one overlapping the final-layer output difference (0.32-0.35 vs 0.03-0.13); two distinct directions argue against both models copying the same letter set. Base copy-suppression head L15h1 is weakened in A. Late MLPs (L13-17) compensate the copy change in each model. Largest QK routing changes are in L10-12. The residual uncertainty is what B's own copy direction carries.
